 Angara pushes condition-based repair strategy for aging classrooms 
 by The Manila Times
 Nov 08, 2026 1:02 pm 
 THE Department of Education (DepEd) clarified that school buildings reaching 50 years of age will undergo detailed, condition-based assessments to safely extend their serviceability through targeted repairs before any decisions on replacement are made.  
 STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY DepEd continues to pursue multi-pronged strategies, including partnerships with local government units (LGUs), private organizations, and other government agencies, to accelerate classroom construction, address historical backlogs, and ensure safe learning spaces nationwide. PHOTO FROM DEPED 
 Addressing reports citing Second Congressional Commission on Education data, which estimate that 51,222 classrooms will hit the 50-year mark by 2028, DepEd emphasized that age alone does not dictate whether a facility must be demolished.  
 Through its Education Facilities Division (EFD), DepEd employs a systematic, risk-informed evaluation framework to assess structures individually and guide budget allocation.  
 Under the DepEd framework, aging classrooms are categorized based on structural readiness. 
 Classrooms in good condition continue to be used and maintained, extending their operational lifespan by an estimated 15 years.  
 Facilities requiring basic maintenance are repaired promptly using Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses funds to add 10 years of serviceability.  
 Structures requiring significant work undergo rehabilitation where technically feasible and safe, extending operational life by five years.  
 Facilities assessed as structurally compromised or beyond repair are scheduled for demolition and replacement.  
 For long-term planning, DepEd projects that 18,132 classrooms per year may require replacement between 2026 and 2030, and 18,380 classrooms per year between 2031 and 2035.  
 Secretary Angara stressed that a sustained repair and rehabilitation budget is essential to preventing premature condemnation and maximizing government resources.
